children: Japanese stocks are likely to be supported next year by reflation, corporate-governance improvements and the capital-expenditure cycle, Morgan Stanley strategists say in a note. A secular bull market in equities, including rising household participation via programs such as Japan's tax-exempt investment program for individuals, is likely to continue in 2027 as nominal GDP growth and return on equity among listed companies improve hand in hand, the U.S. bank says. Morgan Stanley is bullish on Japanese equities and expects the Topix to rise to 4800 by December 2027. The Topix closed Monday at 3901.37. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
